data.overview: Fragonard is a family-owned fragrance and skincare brand founded in 1926 in Grasse, France, with three production factories in southern France. Its own "Fragonard s'engage" page details environmental commitments around recycling, FSC/PEFC-certified paper, and eco-responsible packaging. The independent rating from Good On You scores Fragonard "Not Good Enough" overall (2/5 on planet, people, and animals), noting no evidence of a supplier Code of Conduct, no supplier audits, and no policy against animal testing.

claims.claim: Fragonard says it began an in-depth reflection on environmental and ethical questions in 2018 and recycles cardboard, plastic and glass daily at its three French factories.
claims.quote: Le recyclage du carton, du plastique et du verre fait partie du quotidien de nos usines.

papers.title: Fragonard - Sustainability Rating
papers.summary: Good On You rates Fragonard "Not Good Enough" overall, with 2-out-of-5 scores across planet, people, and animals. It credits some certified organic ingredients and FSC-certified packaging, but finds no evidence of water-reduction action, no Code of Conduct, no supplier audits, no living-wage assurance, and no policy against animal testing. It notes use of insect-derived ingredients.

findings.text: Fragonard uses some lower-impact and certified organic ingredients and FSC-certified packaging, but shows no evidence of meaningful water-reduction action.
findings.quote: It uses some lower-impact ingredients including certified organic ingredients. It uses Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) certified packaging. There’s no evidence it’s taking meaningful action to reduce water use.

findings.text: On labour, there is no evidence Fragonard has a Code of Conduct, audits its suppliers, or ensures living wages.
findings.quote: There’s no evidence it has a Code of Conduct. There's no evidence it audits its suppliers. There’s no evidence it ensures workers are paid living wages in its supply chain.

findings.text: Fragonard has no certification, policy or statement against animal testing, and uses insect-derived ingredients.
findings.quote: It does not have a certification, policy, or statement against the use of animal testing in its supply chain.

findings.text: Fragonard uses ingredients derived from insects such as bee, snail and/or silk byproducts, but no other animal substances.
findings.quote: It uses ingredients derived from insects (eg byproducts of the bee, snail and/or silk industries), but no other animal substances.
